cards.explanation: The answer is a fool whose lips are perverse. Solomon, Israel's king, says a poor man who walks with integrity is better than "…a fool whose lips are perverse." Notice what he's measuring, friends. It isn't the bank account, it's the walk. That's a lot of wisdom packed into one little verse.

The answer is knowledge. "Even zeal is no good without knowledge…" Being fired up is great, friends, but the verse says the one who hurries his footsteps misses the mark. Eagerness needs something to aim with.

The answer is the LORD. The verse says, "A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD." Think about that for a second, friends. The man's own folly wrecked his way, and his heart is mad at the LORD anyway.

The answer is True. Solomon says, "Wealth attracts many friends…" He's pointing at something people notice in real life, friends. Then the verse turns, and it says a poor man is deserted by his friend.

The answer is False. Verse 5 says, "A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who utters lies will not escape." Solomon says it twice in the same verse, friends, just in different words. The liar doesn't get away with it.

The answer is the gift giver. Verse 6 says, "Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver." Everybody wants to be close to the one handing things out, friends. I think Solomon is noticing who people gather around.

The answer is False, and it's a hard one. Verse 7 says he "…may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found." He goes after them, friends, and they're gone. I think that's a lonely picture.
The answer is loving himself. Verse 8 says, "He who acquires wisdom loves himself…" Getting wisdom is the opposite of neglecting yourself, friends. Solomon says it's how a person loves himself.

The answer is success. The verse says the one who safeguards understanding "…will find success." Safeguarding means guarding it like a fresh tray of cookies at a party, friends. And the first half of verse 8 says the one who acquires wisdom loves himself.

The answer is a slave ruling over princes. Verse 10 says, "…how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!" Just before that, Solomon says luxury is unseemly for a fool. He's listing things that don't fit, friends. A fool in luxury is bad enough, and this is worse.

The answer is overlook. The verse says, "A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense." It calls overlooking a virtue, friends. Insight and patience are right there with it.

The answer is False. Verse 12 says, "A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass." See the little word "but" in the middle, friends? The rage is the roar, and the favor is the soft dew.

The answer is a constant dripping. Verse 13 says, "A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping." Anybody who's heard a faucet drip all night knows how that one goes, friends. The picture is about constant quarreling.

The answer is from the LORD. Verse 14 says, "Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD." Houses and wealth can be handed down from fathers, friends. A prudent wife is said to come from the LORD.

The answer is True. Verse 15 says, "Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger." Solomon puts sleep and hunger side by side, friends. Doing nothing leads somewhere, and it's not to a full table.

The answer is True, and it's a serious line. Verse 16 says, "He who keeps a commandment preserves his soul, but he who is careless in his ways will die." Solomon sets two paths side by side, friends. One preserves the soul, and the other is careless.

The answer is a loan to the LORD. Verse 17 says, "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender." Solomon calls kindness to the poor a loan to the LORD, friends. That's a strong way to see a small kindness.

The answer is True. Verse 17 says, "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender." The kindness is treated like a loan, friends, and the person who showed it is the lender. The verse says the LORD will repay. I think that makes a small kindness look a lot bigger than it feels at the time.

The answer is again. Verse 19 says, "A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again." Rescuing him once isn't the end of it, friends. The verse says you will have to do so again.

The answer is so you'll be wise the rest of your days. Verse 20 says, "Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days." Wise for the rest of your days is the goal, friends. That's a long payoff for a little listening.

The answer is False. Verse 21 says, "Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail." Plenty of plans, friends, but one purpose that prevails. And that one belongs to the LORD.

The answer is liar. Verse 22 says, "The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar." Solomon puts being poor ahead of being a liar, friends. That's a plain way to say what matters.

The answer is True. Verse 23 says, "The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm." It leads to life, friends, and to resting content. That's what the fear of the LORD brings, according to Solomon.

The answer is that he won't even bring it back to his mouth. Verse 24 says, "The slacker buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth." The food is right there, friends, and he still won't lift his hand. Solomon makes laziness look pretty silly.

The answer is that he gains knowledge. Verse 25 says, "Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; rebuke the discerning man, and he will gain knowledge." The discerning man takes a rebuke and comes out knowing more, friends. That's a good way to hear a hard word.

The answer is stray. Verse 27 says, "If you cease to hear instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge." Stopping listening is how the drifting starts, friends. Solomon is speaking to "my son" here.

The answer is judgments. Verse 29 says, "Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools." It's a serious line to end the chapter on, friends. Solomon is plain about what's prepared for mockers.

The answer is True. Verse 29 says, "Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools." It's a heavy way to close the chapter, friends. Beatings are named for the backs of fools.
